# Tabs

Generated from the spec. This page is a reference to the contract, not usage guidance.

Switches between related views of the same thing, one at a time, without leaving the page.

Stage: **alpha**. Figma: `Tabs` (mapping not yet confirmed against the Components file). Behaviour: `@radix-ui/react-tabs`.

## Keyboard

Pattern: [WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices: Tabs](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/). Name: The list: list.ariaLabelledby pointing at a visible heading, or list.ariaLabel. Each tab: its label; an icon never gives the name. Each panel: aria-labelledby its tab, set by Radix.

| Key | Part | Does | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tab | list | Moves focus into the list, onto the selected tab. | `tabs-tab-enters-selected` |
| Tab | trigger | Moves focus out of the list to the shown panel. | `tabs-tab-to-panel` |
| Shift+Tab | trigger | Moves focus out of the list to the element before it. | `tabs-shift-tab-leaves-list` |
| ArrowRight | trigger | Horizontal: moves focus to the next tab that is not disabled, wrapping from last to first while list.loop is true. In rtl it moves to the previous tab. Ignored when vertical. | `tabs-arrow-right-next` |
| ArrowLeft | trigger | Horizontal: moves focus to the previous tab that is not disabled, wrapping from first to last while list.loop is true. In rtl it moves to the next tab. Ignored when vertical. | `tabs-arrow-left-previous` |
| ArrowDown | trigger | Vertical: moves focus to the next tab that is not disabled, wrapping while list.loop is true. Ignored when horizontal, so the page still scrolls. | `tabs-arrow-down-next-vertical` |
| ArrowUp | trigger | Vertical: moves focus to the previous tab that is not disabled, wrapping while list.loop is true. Ignored when horizontal. | `tabs-arrow-up-previous-vertical` |
| Home | trigger | Moves focus to the first tab that is not disabled. | `tabs-home-first` |
| End | trigger | Moves focus to the last tab that is not disabled. | `tabs-end-last` |
| PageUp | trigger | Same as Home. Radix adds it; the Authoring Practices do not ask for it. | `tabs-page-up-first` |
| PageDown | trigger | Same as End. Radix adds it; the Authoring Practices do not ask for it. | `tabs-page-down-last` |
| Enter | trigger | Selects the focused tab. With automatic activation the tab is already selected by focus, so Enter changes nothing. | `tabs-enter-selects-manual` |
| Space | trigger | Selects the focused tab, as Enter does. | `tabs-space-selects-manual` |

| MUST | `tabs-required-children` | A tablist contains only tabs. | `axe:aria-required-children` | 1.3.1 |
| MUST | `tabs-list-name` | The list has an accessible name from list.ariaLabelledby or list.ariaLabel; the type of TabsList's props requires one of the two. | `type:tabs-list-needs-name` | 4.1.2 |
| MUST | `tabs-one-selected` | Exactly one tab has aria-selected true at all times. value or defaultValue is required by the type of the props, because Radix starts with no tab selected without one. | `test:tabs-one-selected` | 4.1.2 |
| MUST | `tabs-wiring` | Each tab's aria-controls names its panel's id and each panel's aria-labelledby names its tab's id. | `test:tabs-wiring` | 1.3.1 |
| MUST | `tabs-hidden-panels` | Panels of tabs that are not selected carry the hidden attribute and are not in the accessibility tree. | `test:tabs-hidden-panels` | 1.3.2 |
| MUST | `tabs-icons-hidden` | iconStart and iconEnd carry aria-hidden, so the tab's name comes from its label alone. | `test:tabs-icons-hidden` | 1.1.1 |
| MUST | `tabs-tab-enters-selected` | Tab from the element before the list moves focus onto the selected tab, not the first tab. | `test:tabs-tab-enters-selected` | 2.4.3 |
| MUST | `tabs-panel-focusable` | The shown panel has tabindex 0, so Tab from the selected tab reaches it. | `test:tabs-tab-to-panel` | 2.1.1 |
| MUST | `tabs-shift-tab-leaves-list` | Shift+Tab from any tab moves focus to the element before the list, not to another tab. | `test:tabs-shift-tab-leaves-list` | 2.4.3 |
| MUST | `tabs-arrow-keys` | When horizontal, ArrowRight moves focus to the next tab that is not disabled, wrapping from last to first while list.loop is true, and ArrowUp and ArrowDown do nothing. | `test:tabs-arrow-right-next` | 2.1.1 |
| MUST | `tabs-arrow-left-previous` | When horizontal, ArrowLeft moves focus to the previous tab that is not disabled, wrapping from first to last while list.loop is true. | `test:tabs-arrow-left-previous` | 2.1.1 |
| MUST | `tabs-arrow-down-next-vertical` | When vertical, ArrowDown moves focus to the next tab that is not disabled, wrapping while list.loop is true, and ArrowLeft and ArrowRight do nothing. | `test:tabs-arrow-down-next-vertical` | 2.1.1 |
| MUST | `tabs-arrow-up-previous-vertical` | When vertical, ArrowUp moves focus to the previous tab that is not disabled, wrapping while list.loop is true. | `test:tabs-arrow-up-previous-vertical` | 2.1.1 |
| MUST | `tabs-home-first` | Home moves focus to the first tab that is not disabled. | `test:tabs-home-first` | 2.1.1 |
| MUST | `tabs-end-last` | End moves focus to the last tab that is not disabled. | `test:tabs-end-last` | 2.1.1 |
| MUST | `tabs-rtl-arrows` | In rtl, ArrowLeft moves to the next tab and ArrowRight to the previous one. | `test:tabs-rtl-arrows` | 2.1.1 |

| MUST | `tabs-space-selects-manual` | With activationMode manual, Space selects the focused tab, as Enter does. | `test:tabs-space-selects-manual` | 2.1.1 |

| MUST | `tabs-label-contrast` | In both variants and both themes, every label that is not disabled has at least 4.5 to 1 contrast against what is behind it, including while hovered. | `test:tabs-label-contrast` | 1.4.3 |
| MUST | `tabs-indicator-contrast` | The mark of the selected tab, the brand line in line or the fill in pill, has at least 3 to 1 contrast against the page in light and dark. | `test:tabs-indicator-contrast` | 1.4.11 |
| MUST | `tabs-selected-not-colour-alone` | The selected tab differs from the others by a shape, the line or the fill, and by a heavier label weight, not by colour alone. | `test:tabs-selected-not-colour-alone` | 1.4.1 |
| MUST | `tabs-selected-forced-colors` | In forced colours the selected tab is still marked: the line variant keeps its line and the pill variant shows a 2 pixel border. | `test:tabs-selected-forced-colors` | 1.4.11 |
| MUST | `tabs-list-scrolls-inside` | When the tabs are wider than the list, the list scrolls sideways inside itself. At 320 pixels wide the page has no horizontal scroll. | MUST | `tabs-scroll-region-focusable` | A list that scrolls can be reached and scrolled with the keyboard, which holds because it contains focusable tabs. | `axe:scrollable-region-focusable` | 2.1.1 |

| MUST | `tabs-behavior-fill` | With list.behavior fill, the list is as wide as its container and every tab has the same width, within one pixel; with hug, each tab is as wide as its label and padding. | MUST | `tabs-indicator-edge` | The indicator draws a border width/md thick on one edge only: the bottom edge of the tab when horizontal and the inline-start edge when vertical, along the tab's full length. It is written in the extensions stylesheet; the style rules set only its colour. | `test:tabs-indicator-edge` |  |
| MUST | `tabs-target-size` | Every tab is at least 24 by 24 pixels at every size. | `test:tabs-target-size` | 2.5.8 |
| SHOULD | `tabs-page-up-first` | PageUp moves focus to the first tab that is not disabled, as Radix provides. | `test:tabs-page-up-first` |  |
| SHOULD | `tabs-page-down-last` | PageDown moves focus to the last tab that is not disabled, as Radix provides. | `test:tabs-page-down-last` |  |
| SHOULD | `tabs-selected-in-view-on-mount` | When the list scrolls, the selected tab is scrolled into view when Tabs first renders. (assumption) | `test:tabs-selected-in-view-on-mount` |  |
| SHOULD | `tabs-no-width-shift` | Selecting a tab does not change its width or move the tabs beside it, although the label's weight changes: the extensions stylesheet reserves the width of the heavier weight. (pattern) | `test:tabs-no-width-shift` |  |
| SHOULD | `tabs-touch-target` | Where the pointer is coarse every tab is at least 44 pixels tall. (pattern) | `test:tabs-touch-target` |  |

## Content rules

- One to three words per tab, a noun that names the view: Details, Reviews, Delivery.
- Sentence case. No full stop.
- Labels in one list are parallel in form and similar in length.
- A count, if any, goes in the label in brackets, such as Reviews (124), so it is read as part of the name.
- Do not repeat the list's heading in each label: Delivery, not Delivery options.
- An icon only supports the label; it never replaces it.

## What the spec does not carry

- The live Figma component: its properties were read from a cached copy inside the Semantic Tokens file, which is older than the published library, so every figma mapping here is unconfirmed. That copy has a Tabs set with variant primary or secondary (default primary), behavior hug or fill (default hug), and the switches showOption1 to showOption10 and showScrollShadow; and a tab, _TabsElement, with variant primary or secondary, state default, hover, selected or disabled, orientation horizontal or vertical, a label text property, and prefix and suffix icons with showPrefix and showSuffix switches. The show switches are design-tool switches, not props in code: code renders the tabs and icons it is given.
- Which Figma variant is line and which is pill: Figma calls the property variant with the values primary and secondary, and their looks could not be read. The spec keeps its own names line and pill until the mapping is checked against the library.
- A size property in Figma, and a focus value of Figma's state property: neither is in the copy that could be read, so size and the focus state map to nothing in Figma.
- Layout written in the extensions stylesheet: the list is a row or a column from data-orientation, and the root puts a vertical list beside its panel; the list scrolls sideways inside itself (overflow); each tab lays out its icons and label in a centred row and its label never wraps (white-space); vertical tabs are as wide as the list; the indicator's one-sided border, its edge and its width/md thickness; with list.behavior fill, the tabs share the list's width equally; and each label reserves the width of its heavier selected weight. Each is pinned by a requirement with a test.
- Scroll buttons or fade edges on a list that scrolls, which Figma's showScrollShadow draws. The list scrolls by touch, wheel and keyboard only.
- Badges or close buttons on a tab, and tabs that can be added, removed or reordered by the person using them (the Delete key in the Authoring Practices).
- A tab with a popup menu (Shift+F10 in the Authoring Practices).
- A divider line under the whole list. It is not designed; if added it would be border/primary/default, a divider, written in the extensions stylesheet.
- Motion of the indicator sliding between tabs, and panel transitions. Only a colour transition is specified. Radix's forceMount, which exists for such animation, is not exposed.
- Tabs used as links to other pages: that is navigation with aria-current, a different component.
